0.title: Through the Wilderness: The Book of Numbers
0.overview:
Numbers takes its English name from the two censuses that bracket the book (chs. 1, 26). But the Hebrew title, Bemidbar, "In the Wilderness," tells the deeper truth. This is the book of the in-between, the slow trek from redemption already accomplished at the Red Sea to inheritance not yet received in the Land. It is the story of a people saved out of Egypt but not yet home, and of the God who refuses to abandon them even when they break his heart.

The shape of the book is the shape of a journey gone wrong and grace gone deeper. Israel stands at Sinai, ready to march in eleven days to the Promised Land (Deut 1:2). Then comes the catastrophe of chapters 13–14: the spies, the unbelief, the refusal to trust the God who had split the sea. Forty years of wandering follow, until a generation dies in the desert: a book about faith and the lack of it. Its census totals (1:46) raise an honest question, taken up at chapter 1.

Who wrote Numbers? The book says Moses wrote down the stages of the journey by command of the LORD (33:2), and Jesus and the apostles treat the five books as Moses’ (Luke 24:44). Conservative scholars hold that its substance comes from Moses, with later inspired touches such as 12:3, which speaks of him in the third person; many critical scholars date its final form centuries later. The book’s own claim is the best starting point.

Yet the dominant note is not judgment but astonishing, stubborn mercy. The God of Numbers numbers his people one by one, knowing each by name. He arranges his camp so that his own presence stands at the dead center of their life. He gives the priestly blessing (6:24–26). He sends manna every morning and water from the rock, and when they grumble he disciplines them but never lets them go. The church too is a wilderness people, redeemed but not yet home.

So Paul reaches for Numbers to instruct the church: "Now these things took place as examples for us" (1 Cor 10:6). All of it is written for us, and Hebrews warns the church from the same desert not to harden its heart as Israel did (Hebrews 3:7–19), that we who have begun the journey might finish it in faith. Above every page of Numbers stands the Lord Jesus, the true and faithful Israelite who endured his own wilderness without grumbling, the Rock from whom living water flows, the Serpent lifted up that all who look might live, and the Star that has risen out of Jacob. To read Numbers is to learn how a redeemed people travels home.

1.title: The Census: A People Known by Name

1.overview:
The book opens not with cold statistics but with a tender act of divine knowing. God commands Moses to number his people, and in the numbering we see that the Lord of hosts knows every name, every clan, every father’s house.

The setting is loaded with grace: “in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting.” God speaks to a redeemed people from the place where heaven meets earth. They are barely a year out of Egypt, and already God is organizing them as an army — the people of God on the march toward the inheritance.

The census is military: “all who are able to go to war.” Israel is the LORD’s host, mustered for the conquest of Canaan. Yet the Levites are deliberately excluded from the war count, set apart for a different and higher warfare — the guarding of holy things. From the first chapter, Numbers insists that God is both Commander and Shepherd, counting his sheep by name.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: At Sinai, one month after the tabernacle was raised, the LORD commands a military census of all men twenty and older.
verseByVerse.theology: God speaks from the tent of meeting: revelation flows from the place of atonement. The numbering is an act of covenant ownership.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: a redeemed people mustered as an army. Now: the church is a host on the march, every soldier enlisted by grace.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying, "Take a census of all the congregation of the people of Israel, by clans, by fathers' houses, according to the number of names, every male, head by head. From twenty years old and upward, all in Israel who are able to go to war, you and Aaron shall list them, company by company.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The tent of meeting. Israel has not moved. This is the same mountain where the law was given, and the tent has been standing exactly one month (Exod. 40:17). What has changed is that God now speaks from inside it. From here to the end of the Pentateuch he speaks from the tent in the middle of the camp, where the blood is applied. The address has moved from the mountaintop to the centre of the village.

The first thing he says is: count them, head by head. That phrase governs the whole chapter. This is not a population estimate; it is a roll of names, taken one head at a time, and the tedium of the next fifty verses is the direct result of God refusing to deal with his people in bulk. He calls his own sheep by name (John 10:3) is not a New Testament innovation. It starts in the dust at Sinai.

And it is a muster: the census has a sword in its hand. These men were redeemed out of Egypt for something, and the something involves a fight. Nobody was brought out of slavery to sit down.
verseByVerse.note: Numbers is named for its two censuses (chs 1 and 26). Its Hebrew title is “In the wilderness.” It covers the nearly forty years from Sinai to the plains of Moab.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: A chief from each tribe assists; the tribes are counted one by one, totaling 603,550 fighting men.
verseByVerse.theology: God works through appointed leaders and ordered community. The enormous total fulfills the promise to Abraham.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: each tribe represented, none overlooked. Now: every believer has a place and a representative in the body of Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: And there shall be with you a man from each tribe, each man being the head of the house of his fathers. And these are the names of the men who shall assist you. From Reuben, Elizur the son of Shedeur; from Simeon, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai; from Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab; from Issachar, Nethanel the son of Zuar; from Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon; from the sons of Joseph, from Ephraim, Elishama the son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur; from Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gideoni; from Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai; from Asher, Pagiel the son of Ochran; from Gad, Eliasaph the son of Deuel; from Naphtali, Ahira the son of Enan." These were the ones chosen from the congregation, the chiefs of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the clans of Israel.
verseByVerse.commentary:
God, who knows every one of the six hundred thousand without being told, appoints a dozen men to do the counting. He characteristically does his work through named, accountable people rather than by decree, and the pattern runs all the way to the apostles and elders he gives the church.

The names themselves preach if you listen to them. Most of these names have El (God), Shaddai (the Almighty) or Zur (Rock) built into them, so that a clerk reading the roll aloud at Sinai was confessing the name of God again and again before he reached the end of the list.

One name in the list reaches far beyond it. From Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab. And on the first page of the New Testament: Amminadab the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon the father of Salmon (Matt. 1:4). A clan chief on a wilderness muster roll is the great-great-great-grandfather of David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ. He never knew.

verseByVerse.quote: Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named, and on the first day of the second month, they assembled the whole congregation together, who registered themselves by clans, by fathers' houses, according to the number of names from twenty years old and upward, head by head, as the LORD commanded Moses. So he listed them in the wilderness of Sinai.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Three verses of pure procedure end with the phrase that will become the pulse of the book: as the LORD commanded Moses.

That sentence is repeated in these opening chapters to the point of monotony, and the monotony is deliberate, because of what is coming. This is the book of the rebellion. Within a few chapters the same people will be demanding meat, refusing the land, following Korah and threatening to stone Moses. And the writer establishes, at the front, exactly what the alternative looked like: a nation doing what it was told, on the day it was told, in order.

There is a quiet dignity in the scene: former brick-makers standing in ranks, and nobody is being whipped. They are not doing it because they must; they are doing it because God said so and they still want to. Numbers exists to tell us how a people who began like this ended up buried in a desert — and the first answer is simply that they stopped.

verseByVerse.quote: The people of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Reuben were 46,500. Of the people of Simeon, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, those of them who were listed, according to the number of names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Simeon were 59,300. Of the people of Gad, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Gad were 45,650. Of the people of Judah, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Judah were 74,600. Of the people of Issachar, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Issachar were 54,400. Of the people of Zebulun, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Zebulun were 57,400. Of the people of Joseph, namely, of the people of Ephraim, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Ephraim were 40,500. Of the people of Manasseh, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Manasseh were 32,200. Of the people of Benjamin, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Benjamin were 35,400. Of the people of Dan, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Dan were 62,700. Of the people of Asher, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Asher were 41,500. Of the people of Naphtali, their generations, by their clans, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Naphtali were 53,400. These are those who were listed, whom Moses and Aaron listed with the help of the chiefs of Israel, twelve men, each representing his fathers' house. So all those listed of the people of Israel, by their fathers' houses, from twenty years old and upward, every man able to go to war in Israel— all those listed were 603,550.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Twenty-four verses of the same sentence, twelve times over, and nobody is summarised. God does not compress the small tribes to save space or give Judah extra room for being important. Each of the twelve gets the identical formula and the identical care, which is itself the doctrine the chapter is teaching. His attention does not thin out as the list gets long.

Two of the figures will matter later. Judah is the largest at 74,600, and Jacob had said the scepter would not depart from Judah (Gen. 49:10) — the royal tribe is already the strongest, four centuries before there is a king. And Dan is second at 62,700, which is a sobering thing to know, because Dan will become a byword for idolatry (Judg. 18:30–31) and is missing from the sealed tribes of Revelation 7. A large membership roll has never been the same thing as a faithful church.

The total is 603,550. Set that against the promise made to a childless man outside his tent one night — Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them… So shall your offspring be (Gen. 15:5) — and against the seventy people who went down into Egypt (Gen. 46:27). The number is the receipt: God said a nation, and here is a nation.

And there is a shadow across it that the New Testament will not let us miss. Of these 603,550 men, two will enter the land. With most of them God was not pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness. Now these things took place as examples for us (1 Cor. 10:5–6). Every man in this list was redeemed, counted, armed and enrolled. Being on the register of the people of God is not the same as arriving; what they lacked was faith in the God who had brought them out (Heb. 3:19).

Are the numbers literal? Over 600,000 fighting men implies a people of perhaps two million, and readers rightly ask how so many lived in the Sinai desert. The Hebrew word translated “thousand”, eleph, usually means a thousand, but it can also mean a clan or a military unit (Gideon calls his clan an eleph in Judges 6:15). So some faithful scholars read each tribe’s figure as so many units and so many hundreds, giving an army of perhaps five or six thousand. That would explain why there were only 22,273 firstborn sons (3:43), and why Moses calls Israel the fewest of all peoples (Deuteronomy 7:7). Others answer that the totals add up only as thousands (603,550), and that the census silver of Exodus 38:25–26 matches 603,550 men at half a shekel each exactly. This commentary takes the numbers as written, while granting that the difficulty is real and that Christians who fully trust Scripture differ here. Either way the point stands: God made a nation out of seventy people, and it was God, with manna for forty years, not the desert, that fed them.
verseByVerse.note: The total of fighting men was 603,550 (v. 46).

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Levites are excluded from the military census and appointed to the service and guarding of the tabernacle.
verseByVerse.theology: The Levites stand between the holy God and the people, a mediatorial tribe that foreshadows Christ our great High Priest.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: a tribe set apart to guard holy things. Now: all believers are a kingdom of priests, set apart to serve and to guard the gospel.

verseByVerse.quote: But the Levites were not listed along with them by their ancestral tribe. For the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Only the tribe of Levi you shall not list, and you shall not take a census of them among the people of Israel. But appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings, and they shall take care of it and shall camp around the tabernacle. When the tabernacle is to set out, the Levites shall take it down, and when the tabernacle is to be pitched, the Levites shall set it up. And if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then the pattern breaks: one tribe is taken off the war roll. It reads at first like exclusion and it is the opposite. Three jobs — carry it, care for it, and surround it. When Israel marches they are the removal men; when Israel stops they are the fence.

Before Israel could fight, Israel had to worship, and God took a whole tribe out of the fighting strength to make sure of it. God was content to go into the conquest short-handed rather than have the worship of Israel run by whoever was free that week.

Any outsider. Not the enemy — the outsider, meaning any Israelite who was not a Levite. The fence exists because the thing inside it is lethal to the wrong approach. Hold that beside the moment the curtain of the temple was torn from top to bottom (Matt. 27:51). The rule was not repealed. The distance was closed, from the inside, at the cost of the life of the one Man who could stand in the middle of it.

verseByVerse.quote: The people of Israel shall pitch their tents by their companies, each man in his own camp and each man by his own standard. But the Levites shall camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that there may be no wrath on the congregation of the people of Israel. And the Levites shall keep guard over the tabernacle of the testimony." Thus did the people of Israel; they did according to all that the LORD commanded Moses.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The reason for the ring of Levites is given without euphemism: it is a buffer. God is in the middle of a sinful camp, and between his holiness and their sin he places a tribe. The verb for their duty, the Levites shall keep guard, is the one God used when he put the first man in Eden to work it and keep it (Gen. 2:15). Adam was set to guard a garden where God walked and he let the serpent in. Levi is set to guard a tent where God dwells. Many readers hear an echo here: the vocation Adam dropped is picked up by a tribe with no land of its own.

And the chapter ends where it began, saying twice that Israel did, as though the writer could hardly believe he was able to write it.

Take one last look at that camp before the book takes it apart: a nation in order, doing exactly what it was told. It is the nearest thing to Eden since the gate was shut, and it lasts about ten chapters. Only one man has ever gone the whole distance and been able to say I always do the things that are pleasing to him (John 8:29) — and it is his obedience, not Israel’s and not ours, that finally holds the camp together.

1.theology:
God Knows His People by Name. The census is no bureaucratic exercise but a revelation of the divine Shepherd who counts his flock “head by head.” The same God who numbers the stars (Ps 147:4) numbers his people, and writes the redeemed in the Lamb’s book of life. To be known by God is the foundation of all assurance.

Redemption Unto Warfare. Israel is saved from Egypt not for ease but for battle; the census is a muster of the LORD’s host. So the church is enlisted to fight the good fight of faith, with weapons not of the flesh. Salvation is the beginning, not the end, of conflict.

Holiness Guarded by Mediation. The Levites encircle the tabernacle “so that there may be no wrath.” The holy God cannot be approached carelessly; an outsider who comes near dies. This mediatorial tribe foreshadows Christ, our great High Priest, who alone brings us near and bears away the wrath we deserve.
1.examples:
Then: A redeemed people stood in ordered ranks at Sinai, every man counted and the holy tent guarded at the center.

Now: You are known by God, counted by name, enlisted in his army, and — in Christ — brought near to the holy God who once said “the outsider shall die.” The torn curtain means you are no longer an outsider. Live, then, as one written in heaven’s register, by the Spirit who dwells in you: serve, guard the gospel, and do all that the Lord commands.

2.title: The Camp Arrangement: God at the Center
2.text: <sup>1</sup>The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,<sup>2</sup>"The people of Israel shall camp each by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers' houses. They shall camp facing the tent of meeting on every side.<sup>3</sup>Those to camp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah by their companies, the chief of the people of Judah being Nahshon the son of Amminadab,<sup>4</sup>his company as listed being 74,600.<sup>5</sup>Those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar, the chief of the people of Issachar being Nethanel the son of Zuar,<sup>6</sup>his company as listed being 54,400.<sup>7</sup>Then the tribe of Zebulun, the chief of the people of Zebulun being Eliab the son of Helon,<sup>8</sup>his company as listed being 57,400.<sup>9</sup>All those listed of the camp of Judah, by their companies, were 186,400. They shall set out first on the march.<sup>10</sup>"On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben by their companies, the chief of the people of Reuben being Elizur the son of Shedeur,<sup>11</sup>his company as listed being 46,500.<sup>12</sup>And those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Simeon, the chief of the people of Simeon being Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai,<sup>13</sup>his company as listed being 59,300.<sup>14</sup>Then the tribe of Gad, the chief of the people of Gad being Eliasaph the son of Reuel,<sup>15</sup>his company as listed being 45,650.<sup>16</sup>All those listed of the camp of Reuben, by their companies, were 151,450. They shall set out second.<sup>17</sup>"Then the tent of meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps; as they camp, so shall they set out, each in position, standard by standard.<sup>18</sup>"On the west side shall be the standard of the camp of Ephraim by their companies, the chief of the people of Ephraim being Elishama the son of Ammihud,<sup>19</sup>his company as listed being 40,500.<sup>20</sup>And next to him shall be the tribe of Manasseh, the chief of the people of Manasseh being Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur,<sup>21</sup>his company as listed being 32,200.<sup>22</sup>Then the tribe of Benjamin, the chief of the people of Benjamin being Abidan the son of Gideoni,<sup>23</sup>his company as listed being 35,400.<sup>24</sup>All those listed of the camp of Ephraim, by their companies, were 108,100. They shall set out third on the march.<sup>25</sup>"On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan by their companies, the chief of the people of Dan being Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai,<sup>26</sup>his company as listed being 62,700.<sup>27</sup>And those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Asher, the chief of the people of Asher being Pagiel the son of Ochran,<sup>28</sup>his company as listed being 41,500.<sup>29</sup>Then the tribe of Naphtali, the chief of the people of Naphtali being Ahira the son of Enan,<sup>30</sup>his company as listed being 53,400.<sup>31</sup>All those listed of the camp of Dan were 157,600. They shall set out last, standard by standard."<sup>32</sup>These are the people of Israel as listed by their fathers' houses. All those listed in the camps by their companies were 603,550.<sup>33</sup>But the Levites were not listed among the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses.<sup>34</sup>Thus did the people of Israel. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each one in his clan, according to his fathers' house.
2.overview:
Chapter 2 sets out the camp, and its message is preached by geography: God dwells at the center. The tabernacle stands in the middle, the Levites encircle it, and the twelve tribes are arrayed in four divisions of three, every tent facing inward toward the glory.

This is no sprawl of refugees but a city of God in miniature, and the same divisions that camp together will march together, Judah leading. The God at the center when they rest goes before them when they travel. Where is God? Not distant: he has pitched his tent among his people, which is the trajectory of all redemption, until at last “the dwelling place of God is with man” (Revelation 21:3).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–2 — The Principle: God at the Center
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: God commands that each tribe camp under its own standard, facing the tent of meeting on every side.
verseByVerse.theology: The geography preaches the gospel: God dwells in the midst of his people, the center of their common life.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: tents pitched toward the tabernacle. Now: lives oriented toward Christ, our true center and dwelling place of God.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "The people of Israel shall camp each by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers' houses. They shall camp facing the tent of meeting on every side.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Two clauses set out the whole design of Israel’s life. First: each by his own standard. Every tribe keeps its own banner and its own patch of ground. God does not dissolve the twelve into an undifferentiated mass; Reuben stays Reuben and Dan stays Dan. The people of God are not uniform.

Second, and decisively: facing the tent of meeting on every side. Twelve different banners, and every one of them turned inward toward the same point. The camp is not organised around a leader, a border, a water source or a road. It is organised around an address — the place where God had said he would meet them.

Picture it from above at dusk: a vast square of firelight, with a single tent at the centre and every door pointing at it. That is the shape of a church as well: real difference, held together not by everybody becoming the same but by everybody facing the same way. And it is the shape of the Bible’s closing chapters, where the city is foursquare and has no temple, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb (Rev. 21:22).
verseByVerse.note: The tribes camped in a square around the tabernacle: God dwelt at the centre of his people.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The tribes are arranged in four camps of three: Judah east, Reuben south, Ephraim west, Dan north, with totals for each.
verseByVerse.theology: Judah leads, anticipating the messianic primacy of the Lion of Judah. The whole host is ordered for both rest and march.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: an army arrayed in disciplined order. Now: the church, the army of Christ, set in order under her King.

verseByVerse.quote: Those to camp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah by their companies, the chief of the people of Judah being Nahshon the son of Amminadab, his company as listed being 74,600. Those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar, the chief of the people of Issachar being Nethanel the son of Zuar, his company as listed being 54,400. Then the tribe of Zebulun, the chief of the people of Zebulun being Eliab the son of Helon, his company as listed being 57,400. All those listed of the camp of Judah, by their companies, were 186,400. They shall set out first on the march.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Judah is given two honours, both of placement. The tabernacle’s entrance faced east, so Judah camps at the door, and when the trumpet sounds Judah goes first. No reason is given; it is simply where God puts them.

But Jacob had given the reason on his deathbed: Judah, your brothers shall praise you… The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet (Gen. 49:8–10). There will be no king in Israel for four hundred years, and already, in the marching order of a refugee column, the royal tribe is at the head of the line with the largest division in the camp.

God lays his plans in logistics long before he announces them in prophecy. The tribe that led the march out of Sinai is the tribe of David and of David’s greater Son, and the road ends with a scroll in heaven that nobody can open until somebody says, Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered (Rev. 5:5).
verseByVerse.note: Judah, the tribe of the coming king, camped on the east and led the march.

verseByVerse.quote: "On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben by their companies, the chief of the people of Reuben being Elizur the son of Shedeur, his company as listed being 46,500. And those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Simeon, the chief of the people of Simeon being Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai, his company as listed being 59,300. Then the tribe of Gad, the chief of the people of Gad being Eliasaph the son of Reuel, his company as listed being 45,650. All those listed of the camp of Reuben, by their companies, were 151,450. They shall set out second.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Reuben is Jacob’s firstborn. By ancient convention he should head the column with the double portion, and he is in second place on the southern flank. His father had stated the reason to his face: Unstable as water, you shall not have preeminence, because you went up to your father’s bed (Gen. 49:4). One night, decades earlier, and the birthright went elsewhere permanently. Sin has a long reach.

But Reuben is not expelled or unnamed. He has a standard of his own, a division under it, a place in the square and a chief. God took the preeminence and left the sonship. And the arrangement quietly says what the New Testament says outright, that in the people of God position never rested on birth order: So then it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God, who has mercy (Rom. 9:16). Every one of us lost a firstborn’s standing in Adam, and the only way back is by belonging to the true Firstborn (Col. 1:15).

Gad’s chief is Deuel’s son in 1:14 and Reuel’s here. In Hebrew the letters d and r look almost alike, and some Hebrew manuscripts, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Latin Vulgate read Deuel here too: one man, two spellings.

verseByVerse.quote: "Then the tent of meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps; as they camp, so shall they set out, each in position, standard by standard. "On the west side shall be the standard of the camp of Ephraim by their companies, the chief of the people of Ephraim being Elishama the son of Ammihud, his company as listed being 40,500. And next to him shall be the tribe of Manasseh, the chief of the people of Manasseh being Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur, his company as listed being 32,200. Then the tribe of Benjamin, the chief of the people of Benjamin being Abidan the son of Gideoni, his company as listed being 35,400. All those listed of the camp of Ephraim, by their companies, were 108,100. They shall set out third on the march. "On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan by their companies, the chief of the people of Dan being Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, his company as listed being 62,700. And those to camp next to him shall be the tribe of Asher, the chief of the people of Asher being Pagiel the son of Ochran, his company as listed being 41,500. Then the tribe of Naphtali, the chief of the people of Naphtali being Ahira the son of Enan, his company as listed being 53,400. All those listed of the camp of Dan were 157,600. They shall set out last, standard by standard."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Verse 17 is the pivot of the chapter and of the book: the tent of meeting sets out in the midst of the camps.

Not at the front, like a general, nor behind, like a supply train, but in the middle, on the move as at rest, so that whatever the nation was doing, God was at its centre. That is the Bible’s distinctive claim over every religion of ascent: not a people climbing toward a distant God but a God who has come down and pitched in the middle of the camp, and in the end the Word became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14), where John’s verb means to pitch a tent.

Ephraim goes west, leading Manasseh: Jacob’s crossed hands again, the younger set over the elder (Gen. 48:17–19). Dan goes north with the second largest division and marches last as rear guard: the two strongest bodies are at the head and the tail, with the tabernacle, the families and the flocks between them.

That is a picture of how God keeps his people: the strength on the outside, the vulnerable in the middle. The LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard (Isa. 52:12).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 32–34 — The Total and the Obedience
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The grand total of the host is 603,550; the people camp and set out exactly as the LORD commanded.
verseByVerse.theology: The closing refrain of obedience seals the chapter: the well-ordered people do all that God commands.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: a host that obeyed in every detail. Now: a church, redeemed and indwelt by the Spirit, glad to follow her Lord’s word.

verseByVerse.quote: These are the people of Israel as listed by their fathers' houses. All those listed in the camps by their companies were 603,550. But the Levites were not listed among the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded Moses. Thus did the people of Israel. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each one in his clan, according to his fathers' house.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The totals match chapter 1 exactly, 603,550, with the Levites again counted separately. (On how so large a host could live in the wilderness, and whether the Hebrew word for “thousand” may mean a clan or unit, see the note at 1:20–46.) And for the second chapter running, the book ends on obedience: the settled life and the travelling life both done as he said.

In two chapters a nation of former slaves has been arranged around a tent, every family in a known place, every banner facing inward, the strong at the edges and the holy things in the middle, the whole camp able to move the moment the cloud lifted. It is a picture of what the people of God were made to be.

It is the last time in the book that anything like this can be said. From chapter 11 this same camp is a mob, and most of the men counted here will die in the sand. The order was real and it was not enough. Israel needed a new heart, and the rest of Numbers proves it, until there came one Man in the middle of his people who could say without qualification, I do as the Father has commanded me (John 14:31). His obedience, not ours, is what the people of God finally stand in.

2.theology:
God Dwells in the Midst. The tabernacle stands at the center of the camp, resting or marching: not man’s ascent to a distant God, but God’s descent to dwell among his people.

Order Reflecting Glory. The God of salvation is the God of order; he arranges his people that they may reflect his glory and march as one.

The Primacy of Judah. Reuben forfeited the firstborn’s place, the birthright passing to Joseph and the leadership to Judah (1 Chronicles 5:1–2), and the scepter prophecy takes visible shape, pointing to Christ, who leads his people to the inheritance.
2.examples:
Then: Twelve tribes pitched their tents in order, every banner facing the glory at the center, and moved out at his word.

Now: God has come to dwell among us in Christ before we ever turned toward him, and by his Spirit he lives in his people now. So turn the face of your whole life toward him: keep your God-given identity, yet orient everything around his glory, and march under the Lion of Judah toward the inheritance he secured.

3.title: The Levites as Substitutes: Standing in Place of the Firstborn
3.text: <sup>1</sup>These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.<sup>2</sup>These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.<sup>3</sup>These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.<sup>4</sup>But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the lifetime of Aaron their father.<sup>5</sup>And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,<sup>6</sup>"Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister to him.<sup>7</sup>They shall keep guard over him and over the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, as they minister at the tabernacle.<sup>8</sup>They shall guard all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, and keep guard over the people of Israel as they minister at the tabernacle.<sup>9</sup>And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the people of Israel.<sup>10</sup>And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall guard their priesthood. But if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death."<sup>11</sup>And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,<sup>12</sup>"Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the people of Israel instead of every firstborn who opens the womb among the people of Israel. The Levites shall be mine,<sup>13</sup>for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated for my own all the firstborn in Israel, both of man and of beast. They shall be mine: I am the LORD."<sup>14</sup>And the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,<sup>15</sup>"List the sons of Levi, by fathers' houses and by clans; every male from a month old and upward you shall list."<sup>16</sup>So Moses listed them according to the word of the LORD, as he was commanded.<sup>17</sup>And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.<sup>18</sup>And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.<sup>19</sup>And the sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.<sup>20</sup>And the sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites, by their fathers' houses.<sup>21</sup>To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these were the clans of the Gershonites.<sup>22</sup>Their listing according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward was 7,500.<sup>23</sup>The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle on the west,<sup>24</sup>with Eliasaph, the son of Lael as chief of the fathers' house of the Gershonites.<sup>25</sup>And the guard duty of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting involved the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,<sup>26</sup>the hangings of the court, the screen for the door of the court that is around the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords—all the service connected with these.<sup>27</sup>To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites and the clan of the Izharites and the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites; these are the clans of the Kohathites.<sup>28</sup>According to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, there were 8,600, keeping guard over the sanctuary.<sup>29</sup>The clans of the sons of Kohath were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle,<sup>30</sup>with Elizaphan the son of Uzziel as chief of the fathers' house of the clans of the Kohathites.<sup>31</sup>And their guard duty involved the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which the priests minister, and the screen; all the service connected with these.<sup>32</sup>And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest was to be chief over the chiefs of the Levites, and to have oversight of those who kept guard over the sanctuary.<sup>33</sup>To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites: these are the clans of Merari.<sup>34</sup>Their listing according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward was 6,200.<sup>35</sup>And the chief of the fathers' house of the clans of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.<sup>36</sup>And the appointed guard duty of the sons of Merari involved the frames of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the bases, and all their accessories; all the service connected with these;<sup>37</sup>also the pillars around the court, with their bases and pegs and cords.<sup>38</sup>Those who were to camp before the tabernacle on the east, before the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, guarding the sanctuary itself, to protect the people of Israel. And any outsider who came near was to be put to death.<sup>39</sup>All those listed among the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron listed at the commandment of the LORD, by clans, all the males from a month old and upward, were 22,000.<sup>40</sup>And the LORD said to Moses, "List all the firstborn males of the people of Israel, from a month old and upward, taking the number of their names.<sup>41</sup>And you shall take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—instead of all the firstborn among the people of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the cattle of the people of Israel."<sup>42</sup>So Moses listed all the firstborn among the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded him.<sup>43</sup>And all the firstborn males, according to the number of names, from a month old and upward as listed were 22,273.<sup>44</sup>And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,<sup>45</sup>"Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the people of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle. The Levites shall be mine: I am the LORD.<sup>46</sup>And as the redemption price for the 273 of the firstborn of the people of Israel, over and above the number of the male Levites,<sup>47</sup>you shall take five shekels per head; you shall take them according to the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel of twenty gerahs),<sup>48</sup>and give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who are over."<sup>49</sup>So Moses took the redemption money from those who were over and above those redeemed by the Levites.<sup>50</sup>From the firstborn of the people of Israel he took the money, 1,365 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.<sup>51</sup>And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
3.overview:
Chapter 3 reaches into the logic of the gospel: substitution. On the night of Passover God claimed every firstborn of Israel, spared by the blood of the lamb. Now he takes the tribe of Levi “instead of” the firstborn, one tribe standing in the place of many, and where the Levites fall short in number a redemption price is paid, every life ransomed.

The language is of belonging: God’s saving acts establish his ownership. Aaron’s sons frame the chapter, with the sobering memory of Nadab and Abihu, and every thread (substitution, ransom, belonging) is gathered up in Christ, who redeems his people not with silver but with his own blood.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–4 — The Priestly Line and Its Peril
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The sons of Aaron are named, including Nadab and Abihu who died offering unauthorized fire before the LORD.
verseByVerse.theology: The priesthood is holy and perilous; God must be approached on his terms alone.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: priests who died for strange fire. Now: we draw near only through Christ, the one acceptable mediator.

verseByVerse.quote: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai. These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests. But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the lifetime of Aaron their father.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Only Aaron’s sons are listed. The formula is the one that structures Genesis, these are the generations of, and here it opens a new stage: the founding of a priesthood that will stand between God and Israel. Then, in the middle of the family record, verse 4 comes like a door slamming.

The story is in Leviticus 10. Two of Aaron’s four sons, newly ordained, offered incense God had not asked for: “strange” fire, worship God had not commanded, brought by men entitled to be in the room. Fire came out from before the LORD and they died on the day their ministry began.

The priestly line was nearly extinguished in an afternoon, four names down to two with no grandsons. And this is why it heads the chapter: everything that follows is about who may come near and on whose terms. Numbers 3 is full of words like guard and outsider and put to death, and before any are used the writer shows us two corpses, so that nobody thinks the language is decorative.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 5–39 — The Levites Assigned and Counted
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Levites are given to Aaron for the service of the tabernacle; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are assigned duties and counted at 22,000.
verseByVerse.theology: The Levites are a gift to the priesthood and to the whole people, set apart wholly to the LORD.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: a tribe given over to sacred service. Now: every believer presented as a living sacrifice to God.

verseByVerse.quote: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister to him. They shall keep guard over him and over the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, as they minister at the tabernacle. They shall guard all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, and keep guard over the people of Israel as they minister at the tabernacle. And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the people of Israel. And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall guard their priesthood. But if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death."
verseByVerse.commentary:
The Levites are now brought near and given to Aaron, a different order of nearness. The arrangement is graded: the congregation is served by the Levites, the Levites serve the priests, the priests serve at the altar, and God is at the centre. Every rung is guarded, and the paragraph ends with the fence at the bottom: if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death.

Even the guards are guarded: Aaron and his sons guard their priesthood, an office to be watched over rather than simply possessed. Korah will try to take it in chapter 16, and this verse is already warning him off.

A modern reader resents the fences. They exist because of what is inside them: God really present in a tent in the middle of a camp. No arrangement of curtains and guards was the final answer. The answer was not another fence but a way through: the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain, that is, through his flesh (Hebrews 10:20), made by the only one who could safely stand on both sides of it.

verseByVerse.quote: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the people of Israel instead of every firstborn who opens the womb among the people of Israel. The Levites shall be mine, for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated for my own all the firstborn in Israel, both of man and of beast. They shall be mine: I am the LORD."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Here is the sentence the whole chapter exists to say, and its grammar is in two words: instead of. That is the grammar of the entire Bible, one standing where another should have stood.

God’s claim on the firstborn came from Passover night. Every house in Egypt lost its eldest son except the houses with blood on the doorposts, and in those houses a boy woke in the morning who had no business being alive. From that night, by right of rescue, every firstborn son in Israel belonged to God, not as a figure of speech but as a debt. The spared are owned.

Now God stands an entire tribe in the place of all those sons. The Levites are not more deserving; they are simply where the claim falls instead. Every firstborn boy in Israel lived as a free man because somebody else was carrying his obligation.

Centuries later a poor couple carried a baby into the temple to present him to the Lord (Luke 2:22). He was a firstborn son under this very statute, and he had come to be the substitute.
verseByVerse.note: The Levites stood in place of Israel’s firstborn, whom God had spared in Egypt.

verseByVerse.quote: And the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying, "List the sons of Levi, by fathers' houses and by clans; every male from a month old and upward you shall list." So Moses listed them according to the word of the LORD, as he was commanded. And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari. And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei. And the sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. And the sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites, by their fathers' houses.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The Levites are counted, and the criterion is startling: every male from a month old and upward.

In chapter 1 the qualification was twenty years old and able to go to war; that census asked what a man could do. This one does not ask. A Levite baby of thirty days, who can contribute nothing and carry nothing, is written on the roll, because the roll is not a list of the useful. It is a list of the owned: no probation, no test, on the list because of whose he is.

Anybody who wonders whether they are of any use to God can take heart: the whole tribe was claimed before one of them lifted a tent pole, and the month-old babies were as thoroughly the Lord’s as the men carrying the ark.

verseByVerse.quote: To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these were the clans of the Gershonites. Their listing according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward was 7,500. The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle on the west, with Eliasaph, the son of Lael as chief of the fathers' house of the Gershonites. And the guard duty of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting involved the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the hangings of the court, the screen for the door of the court that is around the tabernacle and the altar, and its cords—all the service connected with these. To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites and the clan of the Izharites and the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites; these are the clans of the Kohathites. According to the number of all the males, from a month old and upward, there were 8,600, keeping guard over the sanctuary. The clans of the sons of Kohath were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle, with Elizaphan the son of Uzziel as chief of the fathers' house of the clans of the Kohathites. And their guard duty involved the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary with which the priests minister, and the screen; all the service connected with these. And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest was to be chief over the chiefs of the Levites, and to have oversight of those who kept guard over the sanctuary. To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites: these are the clans of Merari. Their listing according to the number of all the males from a month old and upward was 6,200. And the chief of the fathers' house of the clans of Merari was Zuriel the son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle. And the appointed guard duty of the sons of Merari involved the frames of the tabernacle, the bars, the pillars, the bases, and all their accessories; all the service connected with these; also the pillars around the court, with their bases and pegs and cords. Those who were to camp before the tabernacle on the east, before the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, guarding the sanctuary itself, to protect the people of Israel. And any outsider who came near was to be put to death. All those listed among the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron listed at the commandment of the LORD, by clans, all the males from a month old and upward, were 22,000.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The work is divided exactly. Gershon camps west and carries the curtains, coverings and hangings: 7,500 men. Kohath camps south and carries the holy vessels, the ark, table, lampstand and altars: 8,600. Merari camps north and carries the structure, down to the pegs and cords: 6,200.

Nobody is left to work out for himself what he is for, and no clan can do without the others: the Kohathites could carry the ark all day and there would be nowhere to put it if Merari had left the sockets behind. The place at the door, facing the sunrise, belongs to Moses and Aaron and the priests (3:38), so that anyone approaching met the mediators first: nobody comes to God except past the priest.

The total is 22,000. (The three clans as printed add to 22,300. An old Jewish answer is that the extra 300 were themselves firstborn Levites, who could not stand in for anyone else; another is a single copying slip, since in Hebrew “three” and “six” differ by one letter, so that Kohath’s 8,600 may first have been 8,300. The chapter’s arithmetic runs on 22,000.)

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 40–51 — The Redemption of the Firstborn
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The firstborn of Israel are counted at 22,273; the Levites stand in for them, and the 273 extra firstborn are redeemed with silver.
verseByVerse.theology: Substitution and redemption price: every life is accounted for, and where the substitute falls short, a ransom is paid.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: silver paid for the surplus firstborn. Now: not with silver but with the precious blood of Christ are we redeemed.

verseByVerse.quote: And the LORD said to Moses, "List all the firstborn males of the people of Israel, from a month old and upward, taking the number of their names. And you shall take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—instead of all the firstborn among the people of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the cattle of the people of Israel." So Moses listed all the firstborn among the people of Israel, as the LORD commanded him. And all the firstborn males, according to the number of names, from a month old and upward as listed were 22,273. And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the people of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle. The Levites shall be mine: I am the LORD.
verseByVerse.commentary:
A second count is taken, of the firstborn sons, and the answer is 22,273. Levites: 22,000. The substitution is two hundred and seventy-three short.

That could easily have been smoothed over, and no one would have known. Instead God has the shortfall counted precisely and will not move on until it is dealt with. He will not have 273 boys in Israel walking about with a claim on them that nothing has answered. Substitution in Scripture is never approximate: one life for one life, counted to the last head.

Only 22,273 firstborn among 603,550 men? That would mean very large families. One common answer is that the count covered only the firstborn born since the Passover, when God claimed them (3:13). Others think it counted only a mother’s first son, and some see here a sign that the large census figures are better read as clans or units (see the note on the Hebrew eleph at 1:20–46). The text does not say, and faithful readers differ.

verseByVerse.quote: And as the redemption price for the 273 of the firstborn of the people of Israel, over and above the number of the male Levites, you shall take five shekels per head; you shall take them according to the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel of twenty gerahs), and give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who are over." So Moses took the redemption money from those who were over and above those redeemed by the Levites. From the firstborn of the people of Israel he took the money, 1,365 shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary. And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the LORD, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verseByVerse.commentary:
So a price is set for the shortfall, five shekels per head, and the total recorded is 1,365 shekels: 273 times five, exactly.

A page of bookkeeping has taught this: God had a claim on every firstborn son, established the night the blood was on the doorposts. He provided a substitute, a whole tribe. And the substitute ran out, and the gap had to be closed with silver.

Then read this: knowing that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your forefathers, not with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot (1 Pet. 1:18–19). Peter does not cite Numbers 3, but he thinks in its terms: a price set for a life. And he says silver was never going to be enough, not for 273, and not for one.

The tribe of Levi could cover 22,000 and no more. There is a Substitute who covers a number no one can count, with no shortfall and no supplementary payment: By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified (Heb. 10:14). The books balanced at Sinai for 1,365 shekels. They balanced at Calvary for ever.
verseByVerse.note: Five shekels was about 2 ounces of silver (ESV note: a shekel was about 2/5 ounce).

3.theology:
Substitution. The Levites are taken “instead of” the firstborn, one in the place of many: the grammar of the gospel, fulfilled when Christ, the true Firstborn, stands in the place of his people and bears the judgment they deserved.

Redemption at a Price. Where the substitute falls short, silver is paid; every firstborn is ransomed. Redemption is never costless.

Belonging to God. God’s saving acts establish his ownership. The redeemed are not their own; they belong, body and soul, to the God who claimed them.
3.examples:
Then: One tribe stood in the place of a nation’s firstborn, and 1,365 shekels ransomed the surplus.

Now: You belong to God by a greater substitution and a costlier ransom. Christ stood in your place; his blood, not silver, paid your release. You are not your own, and the Spirit he has given you is the power to live as one who belongs wholly to the God who redeemed you, even on the days you do it poorly.

4.title: Levitical Service: The Reverent Transport of Holy Things
4.text: <sup>1</sup>The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,<sup>2</sup>"Take a census of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their clans and their fathers' houses,<sup>3</sup>from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who can come on duty, to do the work in the tent of meeting.<sup>4</sup>This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.<sup>5</sup>When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it.<sup>6</sup>Then they shall put on it a covering of goatskin and spread on top of that a cloth all of blue, and shall put in its poles.<sup>7</sup>And over the table of the bread of the Presence they shall spread a cloth of blue and put on it the plates, the dishes for incense, the bowls, and the flagons for the drink offering; the regular showbread also shall be on it.<sup>8</sup>Then they shall spread over them a cloth of scarlet and cover the same with a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles.<sup>9</sup>And they shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all the vessels for oil with which it is supplied.<sup>10</sup>And they shall put it with all its utensils in a covering of goatskin and put it on the carrying frame.<sup>11</sup>And over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue and cover it with a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles.<sup>12</sup>And they shall take all the vessels of the service that are used in the sanctuary and put them in a cloth of blue and cover them with a covering of goatskin and put them on the carrying frame.<sup>13</sup>And they shall take away the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.<sup>14</sup>And they shall put on it all the utensils of the altar, which are used for the service there, the fire pans, the forks, the shovels, and the basins, all the utensils of the altar; and they shall spread on it a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles.<sup>15</sup>And when Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary, as the camp sets out, after that the sons of Kohath shall come to carry these, but they must not touch the holy things, lest they die. These are the things of the tent of meeting that the sons of Kohath are to carry.<sup>16</sup>"And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil, with the oversight of the whole tabernacle and all that is in it, of the sanctuary and its vessels."<sup>17</sup>The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,<sup>18</sup>"Let not the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites be destroyed from among the Levites,<sup>19</sup>but deal thus with them, that they may live and not die when they come near to the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and appoint them each to his task and to his burden,<sup>20</sup>but they shall not go in to look on the holy things even for a moment, lest they die."<sup>21</sup>The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,<sup>22</sup>"Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers' houses and by their clans.<sup>23</sup>From thirty years old up to fifty years old, you shall list them, all who can come to do duty, to do service in the tent of meeting.<sup>24</sup>This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites, in serving and bearing burdens:<sup>25</sup>they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting with its covering and the covering of goatskin that is on top of it and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting<sup>26</sup>and the hangings of the court and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court that is around the tabernacle and the altar, and their cords and all the equipment for their service. And they shall do all that needs to be done with regard to them.<sup>27</sup>All the service of the sons of the Gershonites shall be at the command of Aaron and his sons, in all that they are to carry and in all that they have to do. And you shall assign to their charge all that they are to carry.<sup>28</sup>This is the service of the clans of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and their guard duty is to be under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.<sup>29</sup>"As for the sons of Merari, you shall list them by their clans and their fathers' houses.<sup>30</sup>From thirty years old up to fifty years old, you shall list them, everyone who can come on duty, to do the service of the tent of meeting.<sup>31</sup>And this is what they are charged to carry, as the whole of their service in the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, with its bars, pillars, and bases,<sup>32</sup>and the pillars around the court with their bases, pegs, and cords, with all their equipment and all their accessories. And you shall list by name the objects that they are required to carry.<sup>33</sup>This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari, the whole of their service in the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest."<sup>34</sup>And Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the congregation listed the sons of the Kohathites, by their clans and their fathers' houses,<sup>35</sup>from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty, for service in the tent of meeting;<sup>36</sup>and those listed by clans were 2,750.<sup>37</sup>This was the list of the clans of the Kohathites, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.<sup>38</sup>Those listed of the sons of Gershon, by their clans and their fathers' houses,<sup>39</sup>from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty for service in the tent of meeting—<sup>40</sup>those listed by their clans and their fathers' houses were 2,630.<sup>41</sup>This was the list of the clans of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD.<sup>42</sup>Those listed of the clans of the sons of Merari, by their clans and their fathers' houses,<sup>43</sup>from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty, for service in the tent of meeting—<sup>44</sup>those listed by clans were 3,200.<sup>45</sup>This was the list of the clans of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.<sup>46</sup>All those who were listed of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of Israel listed, by their clans and their fathers' houses,<sup>47</sup>from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come to do the service of ministry and the service of bearing burdens in the tent of meeting,<sup>48</sup>those listed were 8,580.<sup>49</sup>According to the commandment of the LORD through Moses they were listed, each one with his task of serving or carrying. Thus they were listed by him, as the LORD commanded Moses.
4.overview:
Chapter 4 details how the holy things are carried when the camp moves: the Kohathites bear the sacred vessels, the Gershonites the curtains, the Merarites the framework. The most striking note is the danger. The Kohathites must not touch or even look upon the holy things uncovered, lest they die.

The God of grace is also the God of holiness, and his nearness is both Israel’s glory and her peril. The priests cover the holy things before the Levites may carry them; mediation stands between the people and the glory. The chapter humbles us, for we cannot approach God carelessly, and exalts us, for the One who brings us near is Christ, our High Priest, who clothes us so that we may draw near and live.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–20 — The Kohathites and the Holy Things
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Kohathites carry the most sacred vessels, but only after the priests have covered them; to touch or look upon the holy things means death.
verseByVerse.theology: Holiness is perilous; the glory of God must be mediated and covered, lest sinful men be consumed.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: the ark carried under coverings, untouched. Now: we approach the holy God only through Christ, who clothes us to draw near.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "Take a census of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their clans and their fathers' houses, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who can come on duty, to do the work in the tent of meeting. This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
verseByVerse.commentary:
A third census, and a third set of criteria. Chapter 1 counted men who could fight; chapter 3 counted Levites from a month old, because they were owned. This one counts from thirty years old up to fifty years old: the working years, men strong enough to carry a tabernacle across a desert and mature enough to be trusted with it.

A man is claimed as an infant, listed for service in his prime, and released at fifty. Scripture knows a season for heavy work and a season for laying it down, and the God who assigns both is not thereby valuing the man differently.

The Kohathites are given the most holy things: the highest privilege in the camp, and the next sixteen verses are almost entirely about how dangerous it is.

Thirty here, twenty-five in 8:24. The likeliest answer is that Levites entered service at twenty-five and took up the heavy work of carrying the holy things at thirty.

verseByVerse.quote: When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it. Then they shall put on it a covering of goatskin and spread on top of that a cloth all of blue, and shall put in its poles. And over the table of the bread of the Presence they shall spread a cloth of blue and put on it the plates, the dishes for incense, the bowls, and the flagons for the drink offering; the regular showbread also shall be on it. Then they shall spread over them a cloth of scarlet and cover the same with a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles. And they shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all the vessels for oil with which it is supplied. And they shall put it with all its utensils in a covering of goatskin and put it on the carrying frame. And over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue and cover it with a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles. And they shall take all the vessels of the service that are used in the sanctuary and put them in a cloth of blue and cover them with a covering of goatskin and put them on the carrying frame. And they shall take away the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it. And they shall put on it all the utensils of the altar, which are used for the service there, the fire pans, the forks, the shovels, and the basins, all the utensils of the altar; and they shall spread on it a covering of goatskin, and shall put in its poles.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Before a single Kohathite touches anything, the priests go in and cover the ark with the veil, then goatskin, then a cloth of blue, then put in the poles so it can be lifted without a hand coming near it. The table, the lampstand and both altars are wrapped the same way, layer by layer, by priestly hands. The Kohathites arrive to find every vessel already shrouded, and lift poles.

The coverings work in both directions. They protect the vessels from men who are not permitted, and they protect the men from the glory inside. It is not that the ark was fragile. It is that they were.

Nobody comes to the holy God on his own initiative, and nobody handles what is holy except by a way a priest has prepared. Israel could carry the ark because Aaron had gone in first. The church comes to God at all because Jesus has gone as a forerunner on our behalf (Heb. 6:20).

verseByVerse.quote: And when Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary, as the camp sets out, after that the sons of Kohath shall come to carry these, but they must not touch the holy things, lest they die. These are the things of the tent of meeting that the sons of Kohath are to carry. "And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil, with the oversight of the whole tabernacle and all that is in it, of the sanctuary and its vessels." The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying, "Let not the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites be destroyed from among the Levites, but deal thus with them, that they may live and not die when they come near to the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and appoint them each to his task and to his burden, but they shall not go in to look on the holy things even for a moment, lest they die."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then the sentence the chapter has been building to: they must not touch the holy things, lest they die.

These are the men appointed to the job, doing exactly what God told them, and if a hand slips onto the ark itself they die. Centuries later Uzzah put out his hand to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and God struck him down there because of his error, and he died there beside the ark of God (2 Sam. 6:7). He was trying to help. It was still death.

Modern readers find that intolerable, and the honest response is not to explain it away but to notice what is said. Holiness is not a mood; the Bible treats it as something like a live current, real enough to kill, and the poles and coverings exist so that sinful men can work all day within a few feet of it and go home.

God states his motive in verse 19: that they may live and not die when they come near to the most holy things. Every prohibition is there for their survival. God is not looking for an excuse to strike a Kohathite. He is going to enormous trouble so that men who cannot survive his presence unprotected can spend their lives carrying his furniture, and he names each man’s task and burden so that nobody blunders into what was never his to handle.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Gershonites carry the curtains and coverings; the Merarites bear the framework; each is assigned and supervised.
verseByVerse.theology: Every servant has an appointed task; the body of God’s servants is ordered and complete.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: every clan with its assigned burden. Now: every believer gifted and placed in the body of Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers' houses and by their clans. From thirty years old up to fifty years old, you shall list them, all who can come to do duty, to do service in the tent of meeting. This is the service of the clans of the Gershonites, in serving and bearing burdens: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting with its covering and the covering of goatskin that is on top of it and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting and the hangings of the court and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court that is around the tabernacle and the altar, and their cords and all the equipment for their service. And they shall do all that needs to be done with regard to them. All the service of the sons of the Gershonites shall be at the command of Aaron and his sons, in all that they are to carry and in all that they have to do. And you shall assign to their charge all that they are to carry. This is the service of the clans of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and their guard duty is to be under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. "As for the sons of Merari, you shall list them by their clans and their fathers' houses. From thirty years old up to fifty years old, you shall list them, everyone who can come on duty, to do the service of the tent of meeting. And this is what they are charged to carry, as the whole of their service in the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, with its bars, pillars, and bases, and the pillars around the court with their bases, pegs, and cords, with all their equipment and all their accessories. And you shall list by name the objects that they are required to carry. This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari, the whole of their service in the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest."
verseByVerse.commentary:
Gershon takes the fabric of the dwelling, Merari its skeleton, both under the direction of Ithamar. And the Merarites’ loads are assigned by name, down to the pegs. Somewhere in that camp was a man whose whole commission from Almighty God was a bundle of tent pegs, and his name was on a list beside them.

The tabernacle could not stand without the frames, nor the frames without the bases, and the whole structure would come down in a night wind without the pegs and cords. The Kohathite had the more glorious burden, not the more necessary one, and nobody chose which he had.

Every congregation contains Merarites, carrying load-bearing timber nobody looks at, whose absence would be noticed within a week. God assigned that work himself, by name. The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable (1 Cor. 12:22).

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 34–49 — The Levites Numbered for Service
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: The Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites are counted for active service; the total of working Levites is 8,580.
verseByVerse.theology: The obedient ordering of God’s servants is sealed once more: all is done as the LORD commanded.
verseByVerse.examples: Then: a counted host of servants ready for the march. Now: a church equipped and deployed for the work of God.

verseByVerse.quote: And Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the congregation listed the sons of the Kohathites, by their clans and their fathers' houses, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty, for service in the tent of meeting; and those listed by clans were 2,750. This was the list of the clans of the Kohathites, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses. Those listed of the sons of Gershon, by their clans and their fathers' houses, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty for service in the tent of meeting— those listed by their clans and their fathers' houses were 2,630. This was the list of the clans of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD. Those listed of the clans of the sons of Merari, by their clans and their fathers' houses, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come on duty, for service in the tent of meeting— those listed by clans were 3,200. This was the list of the clans of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron listed according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The working Levites are counted clan by clan: Kohathites 2,750, Gershonites 2,630, Merarites 3,200. Beside the six hundred thousand of chapter 1 these are small: the men who carried the dwelling place of God for forty years were fewer than nine thousand. The visible strength of Israel was the army; what made Israel Israel was carried by a fraction of one tribe.

And every one is counted, by clan and task. That is encouragement for anyone whose service is unseen: God has never lost track of who is doing the work.

verseByVerse.quote: All those who were listed of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of Israel listed, by their clans and their fathers' houses, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come to do the service of ministry and the service of bearing burdens in the tent of meeting, those listed were 8,580. According to the commandment of the LORD through Moses they were listed, each one with his task of serving or carrying. Thus they were listed by him, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verseByVerse.commentary:
